extracted.intended_audience: public relations professionals and communications teams (PR pros)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for PR professionals on when and how to craft targeted media pitches and formal press releases, and how to combine them for maximum earned-media impact. Covers formatting, distribution, timing, measurement, and best practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance and personalization
rubrics_metrics.description: A pitch must be relevant to the journalist and their audience; personalization is critical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists receive over 50 pitches a week on average, so the most important factor is relevance to the journalist and their audience. Meticulous research on each media contact's coverage area, topics/beat, preferences, past work, and audience interests is crucial to personalize and tailor pitches appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research media contacts (coverage, beat, preferences)
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand each media contact's coverage area, beats, past work, and audience to tailor outreach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do background research to ensure you pitch story ideas that fit the journalist's interests and make their job easier. The article cites that 68% of journalists said PR pros who take time to understand their audience make their jobs easier.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to pitch — ideal story types
rubrics_metrics.description: Pitching is ideal for stories that tie into breaking news and trends, position your brand as a thought leader, add new angles to prior coverage, or offer exclusives/embargoed news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use pitching when you have unique story ideas, interview opportunities with experts, original research/data related to trending topics, or bylined articles from industry experts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitch objectives (why send a pitch)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pitches aim to generate interest in a story idea and to start strong, long-lasting relationships with journalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasons include proposing unique stories (new products, events, initiatives), offering interview opportunities, providing original research/data, submitting bylined articles. Good pitching can earn coverage and build relationships—making it easier for journalists to work with you.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitch formatting and structure
rubrics_metrics.description: A solid PR pitch should be brief, targeted, and include essential elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical elements: an attention-grabbing subject line; a friendly, professional greeting; who, what, when, where, and why details (two to three paragraphs max); a link to related multimedia assets (photos, videos, logos, etc.); and clear contact info for follow-ups. Today most pitches are emailed, which 9 in 10 journalists prefer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press release purpose and use cases
rubrics_metrics.description: A press release is an official statement broadcasting major announcements to a wide audience, used for product launches, acquisitions, executive hires, events, and significant milestones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Press releases simultaneously share news with media, stakeholders, and the public; can be repurposed into other content; serve as a comprehensive source of truth; and drive website traffic through embedded links. 68% of journalists rely on press releases for content ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to issue a press release
rubrics_metrics.description: Use press releases for publicly sharing major announcements and for mandatory disclosures in regulated industries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best for major public announcements (product launches, acquisitions, executive hires, events) and publishing mandatory disclosures (finance, pharma, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Press release formatting (standard elements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases should follow a standard format so media can quickly reference and use them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard format includes: Headline; Introduction; Body text; Company boilerplate; Contact info. The press release can be distributed via newswire services, company newsrooms, social media, newsletters, dedicated emails to a media list, or through media relationship management platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution channel selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose appropriate channels for press release distribution to reach media, stakeholders, and the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options include newswire services (e.g., PR Newswire), company newsroom, social media, newsletters, dedicated media emails, and media relationship management platforms. Channel choice can affect reach and how journalists discover the release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media advisory vs. press release distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: Media advisories (media alerts) are short updates focused on upcoming events and differ from press releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unlike press releases, media advisories typically include just the basic event details, contact info, and a brief description intended to entice journalists to attend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrated strategy: combine press release and targeted pitching
rubrics_metrics.description: For high-impact PR, use the press release as the authoritative source and send targeted, personalized pitches as teasers that link back to it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issue the press release as the official source of truth with all key details and multimedia assets. Then develop pitches that highlight the most interesting data points, quotes, and story angles tailored to each journalist, including a link to the press release to keep pitches short. Repurpose approved release content into blogs, social posts, paid ads, and other formats to amplify the message.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shared best-practice tips for both pitching and releases
rubrics_metrics.description: Techniques that improve both pitches and press releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create attention-grabbing subject lines/headlines; incorporate relevant data and quotes; tell a compelling brand story; use multimedia assets (photos, logos, videos, infographics); align messaging across channels (website, social, sales); and optimize press releases for SEO with relevant keywords and alt text for graphics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metrics to track PR impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Move beyond counts of sends/releases to metrics that show real impact on media coverage and business outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pitching metrics to track: open and response rates from targeted journalists; earned media placements; total potential reach and audience of placements. Press release metrics to track: total release pick-ups and coverage views; website traffic increases from the release (views, click-throughs, sign-ups, downloads); social media engagement (shares, impressions, etc.). Tie PR metrics to organizational KPIs to demonstrate business impact.
